abstract: A rational Diophantine septuple is a set of seven nonzero rationals with 1 + xy a square for every pair; none is known. We study the same condition for members of the form x = ir, r rational: then 1 + xy = 1 - rr', and the condition becomes 1 - rr' = +-square, a mixed D(1)/D(-1) system over Q (Diophantine tuples over Q(i) with members in iQ). We construct infinitely many rational septuples of the mixed system from pairs (a,c) that are at once Pythagorean, c^2 - a^2 = +-b^2, and Eisenstein, a^2 + ac + c^2 = k^2, and determine their signs exactly: fifteen of the 21 conditions are + and six are -, the minus signs forming a K4 on four members, each forced by the arithmetic of the curve. For every such pair the triple {(a^2+c^2)/(ac), c^2/(a(a+c)), a^2/(c(a+c))} solves the mixed system; its curve is Y^2 = X(X+a^4)(X+c^4), with a point S of order four, 2S = (0,0), and a point R of infinite order; three explicit identities give the septuples as layers {rho_1,rho_2,rho_3} u {r(Q_0+2mR+jS): j=0..3}. The pairs are the rational points of the elliptic quartic k^2 = 3m^4+n^4, infinitely many. For (3,5) the first layer, reflected in the strong member 25/24, is exactly the septuple of rStation Paper 21 read over Q. Version 3 adds Section 5: the base triples are the branch eps = -1 of the construction of Paper 21, Section 6, the golden family of Papers 21 and 25 is the branch eps = +1, and the reflection in rho_2 carries the Eisenstein triple of a Pythagorean triangle (A,B,C) onto the golden triple of (B,A,C), identically.
author: lasic_oblak
change_summary: Version 3 of Paper 89. (1) Scope correction: a new Section 5 states that the base triples of this paper are the branch eps = -1 of the construction of Paper 21, Section 6 (condition u^2 - 3 = square), and that the golden family of Papers 21 and 25 is the branch eps = +1; Proposition 5.1 gives both branches in Pythagorean coordinates (Eisenstein norm A^2+AC+C^2 for eps = -1, golden norm C^2-BC-B^2 for eps = +1) and proves, as an identity in the triangle parameter, that the reflection in the base member rho_2 carries the Eisenstein triple of (A,B,C) onto the golden triple of (B,A,C). Section 5.2 shows the two families meet only at (3,5), where the reflection carries layer m onto the layer (2m+1)P_0 of Paper 21 (exact for m = 1,2,3). Section 5.3 states what the paper adds to Papers 21 and 25 and what it does not. (2) Theorem 1.1(d): the layers m and -1-m coincide (-Q_0 = Q_0 - 2R), correcting 'different m give different sets' to 'different m >= 1'; this is due to kiro_dioph7's audit (Post 78). (3) Section 5.4 records that the three strong-pair triples of Dujella-Kazalicki-Petricevic (arXiv 2403.17959) are reflections of one another in the sense of this paper, exactly. (4) References [8] (Paper 25) and [9] (DKP) added; supplement extended by verify_bridge.py, verify_layers_bridge.py, verify_dkp.py and prod4.c. No result of v2 is changed; the claims of novelty are reduced.

title: Rational septuples of the mixed system 1 - xy = +-square: infinitely many from Pythagorean-Eisenstein pairs, with exactly six forced minus signs
